jobs.title: Director, Personal Lines, Business Planning & Performance
jobs.description:
Job ID:
10365

Employment Type:
Existing Role

Work Environment:
We offer a hybrid work environment that offers flexibility to our employees in balancing in-office (2 days per week OR 15 hours per week in a Wawanesa office) and remote work. You may work from any of the following locations: Winnipeg, MB; Calgary, AB; oronto (North York), ON; Kitchener.

Working Business Language
: English

Salary:
At Wawanesa, salary is only one component of a holistic, comprehensive and competitive offering that we provide to our employees. In addition to salary, full-time and part-time permanent employees are eligible for an annual bonus plan, leave of absence top-up programs and provided with generous vacation time, personal days, premium free benefits and pension plan.

The salary offered for this role is determined with consideration to various factors, including but not limited to: your work location, local labour market conditions, external market salary data, internal pay equity and the knowledge, skills, experience and anticipated proficiency in the role. The salary offered is estimated to be within the following range: $120,000 - $140,000. Candidates with salary expectations outside of the range are still encouraged to apply.

About The Wawanesa Mutual Insurance Company

Founded in 1896, The Wawanesa Mutual Insurance Company is one of Canada’s largest mutual insurers, fully owned by its more than 1.8 million members. Headquartered in Winnipeg, Wawanesa is the parent company of WSI™, a specialty insurer delivering tailored solutions built around unique needs; Wawanesa Life, a provider of life insurance products; and Western Financial Group, a leading national distributor of personal and commercial insurance.

Wawanesa is committed to helping communities thrive in a changing world. The company invests more than $4 million annually in charitable initiatives, including $2.5 million each year to support people and communities on the front lines of climate change. Learn more at wawanesa.com.

We are currently seeking dedicated, driven, and enthusiastic individuals who thrive in a dynamic environment, embrace change, and are eager to gain diverse experience while advancing their careers as part of a growing team.

Job Overview

The Director, Personal Lines, Business Planning & Performance is responsible for coordinating business strategy and planning development, providing trusted advice, insights and performance management across the Personal lines of business and key business partners.

This role provides critical support to the SVP & Chief Personal Lines Officer by monitoring market developments and gathering internal and external performance metrics and business insights to enable informed decision-making, identifying opportunities for improvement, and ensuring enterprise-level alignment in planning, reporting, and execution. This role also brings together pertinent information (performance metrics, business insights and market data) into a cohesive view and narrative for the Line of Business for Executive and Board reporting. With direct leadership of cross functional business planning and market monitoring, this role is instrumental in building a performance-focused and member-centric culture. This role requires balancing high-level strategic work with tactical execution, ensuring focus on achieving Wawanesa’s critical goals in the coming years.

Job Responsibilities

Serve as an advisor to the Chief Personal Lines Officer, delivering confidential counsel and perspective on matters of priority to Personal Lines planning and performance across the line of business.
Coordinate the Personal Lines strategic and tactical business planning process, gathering the relevant operational reporting/performance monitoring inputs, ensuring alignment with enterprise planning processes and priorities.
Collaborate closely with executive leadership to translate strategic objectives into measurable initiatives and performance indicators. Oversee the design and execution of executive reporting dashboards, business reviews, and decision-support analytics for the SVP and senior leadership.
Monitor and analyze external competitor and market developments, industry benchmarks, and risk, to present actionable information to support decision-making and prepare the organization to adapt effectively and proactively to changes.
Foster a collaborative environment that brings together sales, operations, finance, compliance, legal, and strategy to address performance and planning needs holistically.
Drive cross-functional initiatives and deliver results by executing through influence, effectively navigating a matrixed structure without direct authority.
Create and manage agendas and execute logistics for Personal Lines Senior Leadership meetings (including strategy and offsite sessions), Personal Lines communication forums (e.g., Townhalls, Ask Anything sessions, etc.) and track follow-ups.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business, insurance, actuarial science, analytics, or a related field; MBA or equivalent advanced education is an asset.
Minimum 8–10 years of experience in strategic or business planning, performance reporting, operational leadership or regulatory compliance in the P&C insurance industry.
Proven leadership experience managing cross-functional teams and delivering results in a matrixed environment.
Strong understanding of insurance operations, risk management and industry financial and non-financial performance drivers.
Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into action, drive execution, and measure impact through well-structured performance frameworks, including analyzing complex issues from multiple angles and provide sound counsel among competing priorities.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, with a high degree of comfort working with data, financials, and reporting tools.
Exceptional versatility, agility, situational awareness, and composure. Proven ability to navigate multiple issues concurrently and prioritize critical work.
Demonstrated ability to analyze complex issues from multiple angles and provide sound counsel among competing priorities, including experience in financial literacy and quantitative analysis, with the ability to distill actionable insights.
Effective communicator and collaborator, with strong storytelling and presentation skills and the ability to influence senior stakeholders.
Deep alignment with Wawanesa’s values and purpose, with a passion for supporting people, protecting members, and improving the way we work.
Flexibility to travel within Canada and work variable hours, including overtime, as required.
Agile business mindset with a focus on innovative problem-solving and interdepartmental collaboration.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including executive-level correspondence.

Diversity Equity, Inclusion & Belonging

At Wawanesa, we are committed to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) and believe that our strength lies in the diversity of our people – this is supported by having a representative workforce.

We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, including racialized persons, women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, members of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, gender-diverse and neurodiverse individuals, and anyone who can contribute to the further diversification of thought and ideas.

We aim to ensure our recruitment process is accessible to all candidates. If you require accommodations during any stage of the recruitment process, please reach out in confidence to jobs@wawanesa.com.

All Wawanesa job applicants are subject to Wawanesa's Privacy Policy.

Please note that the recruitment process for this position may involve the use of AI tools to screen, assess, or select applicants. All final decisions are taken or reviewed by human recruiters and human hiring leaders in compliance with all applicable legislation.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Our client is a well-established and growing organization in the CPG manufacturing and distribution sector. While they continue to expand their operations, strengthen market presence, and drive long-term growth, they are seeking an accomplished Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to join their executive leadership team.
Reporting directly to the President, the CFO will serve as a key strategic partner, providing financial leadership, business insight, and operational support across the organization. This executive will play a critical role in driving profitability, optimizing financial performance, supporting growth initiatives, and ensuring strong financial governance within a fast-paced CPG manufacturing and distribution environment.

Immediate Vacancy
On-site work space

What Our Client Offers
Competitive base salary of $210,000 to $240,000, with flexibility to consider a higher compensation package for an exceptional candidate.
Annual performance-based bonus opportunity of 20% to 25%.
Three weeks of vacation, with the potential for four weeks based on experience and qualifications.
Comprehensive health and dental benefits.
Retirement savings program.

Your Impact in the Company

Lead the organization's overall financial strategy, planning, and performance.
● Provide financial insight and recommendations to the CEO and executive leadership team.
● Oversee budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and cash flow management.
● Drive profitability through margin analysis, cost optimization, and operational efficiencies.

Partner with Operations, Supply Chain, Sales, and Distribution teams to support business objectives.

Manage banking relationships, financing activities, and capital planning.

Ensure strong internal controls, risk management, and regulatory compliance.

Lead and develop the Finance and Accounting teams.

Support strategic initiatives, acquisitions, and business growth opportunities.

Qualifications for this position

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; MBA considered an asset.
CPA designation is a strong asset.
10+ years of progressive senior financial leadership experience, including experience as a CFO, VP Finance, or equivalent executive-level role.
Experience within the consumer products industry
Strong understanding of cost accounting, inventory management, production costing, and supply chain finance.
Proven success leading financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, and business performance management.
Experience managing lender relationships, capital planning, and cash flow optimization.
Strong knowledge of financial reporting, corporate governance, risk management, and internal controls.
Strong leadership capabilities with the ability to influence and collaborate across all levels of the organization.

After submitting your resume, you will receive a reach out from our virtual recruiter. This reach out contains an important questionnaire that must be completed to highlight your skills for this position. We will contact qualified candidates for this role.

AI (Artificial Intelligence) tools may be used at certain points of the pre-screening and selection process for this role. To learn more about ABL's AI policy, please visit www.ablemployment.com/how-abl-utilizes-automation-and-ai-technology/

jobs.title: Director of Finance And Accounting
jobs.description:
Company Description
Refine Finance provides AI-powered fractional CFO and outsourced accounting services that deliver expert financial guidance at a fraction of the cost of a full-time in-house team. The company helps small and mid-sized businesses automate routine financial tasks, access real-time strategic insights, and make data-driven decisions to support efficient growth. With advanced AI-driven analytics, clients can optimize cash flow, forecast trends, manage risk, and maintain compliance and financial accuracy. Refine Finance serves entrepreneurs and business owners across North America, taking leadership of their finances, operations, and strategy so they can focus on scaling their businesses and ensuring long-term financial health.
Role Description
The Director of Finance and Accounting is a full-time, hybrid role based in the Greater Toronto Area, Canada, with flexibility for some work from home. This role oversees financial planning and analysis, budgeting, forecasting, and the preparation and review of financial statements and reports. The Director will manage accounting operations, ensure accuracy and compliance with relevant standards and regulations, and optimize internal controls and financial processes. Day-to-day responsibilities include leading and mentoring a finance and accounting team, providing strategic financial insights to support decision-making, partnering with leadership on growth initiatives, and leveraging data and technology to improve efficiency and financial visibility. The Director will also communicate financial performance and risks to stakeholders and contribute to long-term financial strategy and governance.
Qualifications

Strong expertise in Finance and Financial Planning, with experience in budgeting, forecasting, and strategic analysis.
Proficiency in preparing and reviewing Financial Statements and Financial Reporting, including compliance with accounting standards and regulatory requirements.
Demonstrated Analytical Skills and the ability to interpret complex financial data to provide clear, actionable insights.
Proven leadership experience managing finance and accounting teams, including coaching, performance management, and team development.
Advanced skills with financial systems, spreadsheets, and data analysis tools; experience with AI-driven or automated finance platforms is an asset.
Solid understanding of internal controls, audit processes, risk management, and best practices in corporate governance.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present financial information to non-financial stakeholders and build strong cross-functional relationships.
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related field; CPA, CFA, or equivalent professional designation strongly preferred.
QBO experience is a must
Project based accounting is a plus

jobs.title: Director of Sales Strategy and Solution Design
jobs.description:
*Current or previous experience in the Staffing & Recruitment industry is required for this position*

About the role

The Director will support the Vice President Sales as a trusted advisor. As a strategic thinker this individual brings operational experience executing on key sales focus areas. The Director is a strategic and critical role responsible for working closely with business development and account expansion leaders to drive key strategic initiatives and delivering profitable solution design. The director leads the analysis and architecture of client solutions by assessing the client’s requirements, developing and validating solution design.

What you’ll be doing

Oversees solution design and provides support for business development and account expansion opportunities.
Assesses client business needs, goals and overall strategic direction.
Leads the analysis and architecture of client solutions.
Develops and validates solution design/blueprint.
Collaborates with internal business partners to develop profitable account design recommendations.
Stays abreast of industry/market knowledge and trends.
Improves the probability of RFP wins for strategic deals by incorporating solution design to create opportunity tailored value propositions for every bid.
Collaborate with Vice President, Sales to ensure execution of agreed goals and initiatives.
Ensure proactive management of key relationships both internally and externally (employees, executives, clients, industry organizations, etc).
Identify pain points throughout the sales organization and optimize processes and procedures to improve efficiencies across teams.
Represent company as required, including at industry events and conferences.
Support the Vice President, Sales in preparation for corporate meetings, and meetings with key external stakeholders, including customers, and strategic partners
Partner with the Vice President, Sales to develop and drive key strategic initiatives that support the long-term growth and success of the business.
Facilitate cross-functional collaboration ensuring successful execution of key projects and initiatives.
Provide expert analysis, insights, and recommendations on a wide range of business topics, including market trends, competitive threats, and emerging opportunities.
Prepare and deliver reports, presentations, and other materials to support the Vice President, Sales in decision-making and problem-solving.
Participates in special projects and performs other duties as assigned.

About you

Completion of post-secondary education in related field or years of equivalent experience demonstrating progressive responsibility.
A minimum of eight (8) years of related experience, preferably within the service sector.
A minimum of three (3) years in a management or leadership role.
Proficient in Microsoft Office products including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams and Outlook.
Bilingualism (English & French) is an asset.

BEHAVIOURAL COMPETENCIES:
Strong leadership skills. Can effectively develop and articulate both short-term and long-term business strategies, influencing and motivating others towards such goals.
Strategic orientation with a solid understanding of how the strategies help drive the bottom line.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, both written and verbal, both one-on-one and in group settings.
Able to gather, consolidate and evaluate information, identify key issues, draw conclusions and devise solutions based on sound, practical judgment, experience and operational knowledge.
Demonstrated business professionalism, respect for confidentiality and experience handling sensitive information.
Superior organizational skills. Can effectively manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment and meet deadlines consistently while maintaining high levels of attention to detail.
Demonstrated ability to work across all levels of the organization to obtain resources and provide support and expertise.
Strong planning, research, and project management skills. Proactive and able to solve problems effectively and rapidly using excellent analytical skills.
Proven consistently high levels of customer service performance.
Flexible and adaptable to changing business needs, with an ability to travel when required.

Why choose us?

It’s an exciting time to be part of our team. We’re proud to be a global thought-leader and care about doing the best job we can to ensure better futures for everyone. We do this by building our Future@Work strategy as a united team of 30,000+ colleagues with a collective spirit working in over 60 countries globally.

You’ll have the opportunity to grow across a variety of interesting jobs and careers over our extensive portfolio of global brands. We empower our colleagues to work in the smartest, most efficient ways to achieve total balance between the demands of their jobs and their lives. That’s why we give you the autonomy and support you need to work in the way that makes you most productive, agile, confident and insightful.

Putting people first, pioneering with a collective spirit and always advancing with a growth mindset - that’s what we stand for at the Adecco Group. Here, we are all individuals with a unique perspective on the world we live in. That’s what makes us stronger. Whoever you are and whatever your background, you can be yourself. So, we aim to build on the attributes that make you, you. We offer a range of world-class resources for upskilling and development, satisfying your curiosity while sharing skills, knowledge and expertise to grow together.
Do you want to make an impact where it matters most? Apply NOW!

A journey to bring out the best in you

We believe that having an understanding of the hiring process helps you to prepare, feel, and be at your best. As a global, multi-brand organisation with many different roles, our application process can vary.

On our career site, you will find some of the key steps you can expect to guide you along the way.
As one of the world’s largest employers we believe in talent, not labels, and focus on the diverse and unique skills our people bring. We seek to foster a culture of belonging and purpose, an environment where everyone can thrive and feel engaged, and where difference is respected and valued.
Our commitment to equity, equal opportunity, inclusion, and diversity is part of our broader commitment to respecting fundamental human rights across our value chain.
The Adecco Group is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Salary & Additional Information

*This position is for an existing vacancy.
* The posted range (Base Salary) for this position is between $90,000-$120,000 per annum.
